The name Analika carries the meaning “Intelligent, Spear” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. historical_references.reference: Analika was a famous princess of the Vatsa kingdom in ancient India during the 6th century BC. She is best known for her role in the story of the Buddha's first visit to Magadha, where she is said to have met the Buddha and offered him her park, the Grove of Nigrodha, for a monastery.

Analika is also mentioned in the Jataka tales, a collection of Buddhist stories, as the wife of King Mahanama of Kosala. In one story, she is praised for her generosity and hospitality towards the Buddha and his companions during their travel in her kingdom.
